primary_article.title: Switching immunoglobulin products, what are the implications? Result of 2018 census of immunology centres

supplement.title: National Framework Agreement for Human Immunoglobulins (Supplementary material S1)
supplement.classification: supplementary policy/commissioning document; not primary study evidence

findings: Three Table 1 redness/itch entries are intentionally retained as distinct reported cases because they occupy separate table rows.
Aggregate reaction-count atoms are retained alongside individual table-row adverse-event atoms because they represent distinct source assertions.

extraction_limitations: The article reports 802 product switches but does not establish that these represent 802 unique patients; atoms therefore describe switch events rather than unique-patient counts.
The census was retrospective and centre-reported; individual patient-level source records and adjudication were not available in the retrieved files.
The supplementary NHS England framework is a policy/commissioning document rather than primary research; its atoms are tagged non_primary_source and use a separate publication_id.
No funding, conflict-of-interest, or data-availability statement was visible in the retrieved article PDF; none was invented.
Product-specific commissioning recommendations in the 2017 supplement are historical and were not externally updated for current practice in this extraction.
source_consistency_findings: Supplement S1 contains inconsistent product spellings across its table and narrative (for example Panzyga/Penzyga, Cuvitru/Civutro/Civitru, and Gammagard/Gamagard). Canonical product names in affected atoms are normalized from the table and those atoms are marked assertion_origin=normalized_from_source.
schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated atom kind for policy/guideline recommendations; supplementary policy statements are represented as atom_kind=other with descriptive tags.
